Ken Paxton

Republican candidate for U.S. Senator, Texas · Open seat

Texas Attorney General

Ken Paxton has been Texas attorney general since 2015. Before that he served 10 years in the Texas House and two years in the Texas Senate, representing the McKinney area. He won the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate over incumbent Sen. John Cornyn, was impeached by the Texas House in 2023 and was acquitted on all charges by the Texas Senate.

Where Paxton stands

Gas tax
Supports permanently repealing the federal gas tax. Supports keeping regulations on the oil and gas industry low and says more U.S. production will lower prices.
Data centers
Supports more data center development in Texas with conditions, saying there is "plenty of open space" for them. Has called his position "a yes with conditions."
Border wall in Big Bend
Said building roads and barriers in Big Bend is "not smart border security" and said he "fully supports" the federal decision to pause construction.
Federal spending
In a leaked recording of a private fundraiser, suggested he would support cuts to federal benefit programs to reduce the national deficit.
Cryptocurrency
Supports a "pro-growth" regulatory framework for cryptocurrency and wants the U.S. to lead in digital assets.
Iran and war powers
Backs the president's actions on Iran; says he will decide on funding after getting more intelligence.
Gender care for minors
Opposes it; as attorney general he extended the state ban to mental health providers.
Marijuana and hemp
Has sued Dallas over marijuana decriminalization; no direct comment found on Texas THC rules.
